app-icon.title: App Icon Generator
app-icon.upload-description: Upload a 1024x1024px PNG image to generate icons for all platforms.

source.title: Preparing the source image
source.description: Every size is produced by downscaling a single source image, so the quality of that one file determines the quality of the whole set. Start at 1024 × 1024 — the size the App Store requires — and let the generator produce everything below it.

list.1: Square, at least 1024 × 1024 pixels. Anything smaller will be upscaled and will look soft on modern displays.
list.2: PNG, with no transparency if the icon is destined for iOS.
list.3: Artwork that survives being shown at 48 × 48 — fine detail and thin strokes disappear at the smallest sizes.
list.4: No rounded corners or drop shadows of your own; both platforms apply their own mask.
list.5: Colour in sRGB. Wide-gamut profiles can shift noticeably once the OS re-renders the icon.

ios.title: iOS icon sizes
ios.description: Xcode asset catalogues expect a specific file for each device and scale factor. The 1024 × 1024 image is the one submitted to App Store Connect; the rest are used on-device.

android.title: Android icon sizes
android.description: Android resolves icons by density bucket rather than by device. Each mipmap folder holds the same icon at a different resolution, and the launcher picks the one matching the screen.

rows.play-store: Store listing artwork, uploaded separately from the APK or bundle
rows.xxhdpi: ~480 dpi — common mid-range and older flagships

adaptive.title: Adaptive icons
adaptive.description: Android 8.0 and later composites a foreground and background layer and applies a device-specific mask, which may be a circle, squircle or rounded square. Keep the meaningful part of the artwork inside the central 66% of the canvas, because everything outside that can be cropped on some devices.

pitfalls.title: Common mistakes
pitfalls.description: Store review rejections and odd-looking icons almost always trace back to one of these.

alpha.problem: App Store Connect rejects the icon for containing an alpha channel
alpha.fix: iOS icons must be fully opaque. Flatten the image onto a solid background and re-export as PNG without transparency.

rounded.problem: The icon appears with doubled or clipped corners
rounded.fix: Supply a full square. Both platforms apply their own corner mask, so pre-rounded artwork gets rounded twice.

safe-area.problem: Part of the artwork is cut off on some Android devices
safe-area.fix: Adaptive icon masks vary by manufacturer. Keep logos and text within the central 66% of the canvas.

text.problem: The icon is unreadable on the home screen
text.fix: Wordmarks that read well at 1024 px are illegible at 48 px. Use a symbol rather than text, and check the smallest export before shipping.

upscaling.problem: The icon looks blurry on high-density screens
upscaling.fix: The source was smaller than 1024 × 1024 and has been upscaled. Re-export from vector artwork at full size rather than enlarging a raster file.

overview.title: What a web app manifest does
overview.description: The manifest is the JSON file that turns a website into something installable. Chrome reads it to decide whether to offer the install prompt; Android reads it for the launcher icon and splash screen; iOS reads part of it for the home screen.

required.title: What Chrome requires before it will offer installation

items.manifest: A linked manifest that is served as JSON
items.name: Both name and short_name
items.display: A display mode of standalone, fullscreen or minimal-ui

sizes.title: Icon sizes and what uses them

maskable.title: Maskable icons
maskable.description: Android reshapes launcher icons into a circle, squircle or rounded square depending on the device. A normal icon gets a white box drawn behind it. A maskable icon fills the whole canvas and keeps its important artwork inside a centred circle covering 80% of the width — the outer 20% is padding the system may crop away.

noPrompt.fix: Check that the manifest is linked in the head, returns 200, has 192 and 512 icons, and that the site is on HTTPS. Chrome DevTools → Application → Manifest lists what is missing.

whiteBox.problem: The Android icon has a white box around it
whiteBox.fix: You are missing a maskable icon. Add one with purpose set to maskable.

opensInBrowser.problem: The installed app opens in a browser tab
opensInBrowser.fix: start_url is outside scope, or display is set to browser.

wrongSplash.problem: The splash screen is the wrong colour
wrongSplash.fix: background_color paints the splash before the app renders; theme_color paints the status bar.

hash.description: Compute MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 for text or a file, and compare against a published checksum. Nothing is uploaded.

warning.broken: {algorithm} is broken and must not be used for signatures, passwords or integrity against a motivated attacker. It is fine for checking a download against a published checksum.

overview.title: What a hash is for
overview.description: A hash turns any input into a fixed-length fingerprint. The same input always produces the same digest, and changing a single byte changes the whole thing. That makes hashes useful for confirming a file arrived intact, not for storing passwords.

verify.title: Verifying a download
verify.description: Projects publish a checksum next to the download. Hash the file you received and compare. The tool accepts the sha256sum output format, so you can paste the whole line including the filename.

steps.download: Download the file and its published checksum
steps.hash: Drop the file in above and pick the matching algorithm
steps.compare: Paste the published checksum into the compare box
steps.confirm: A green match means the bytes are identical

passwords.title: Do not hash passwords with these
passwords.description: MD5, SHA-1 and even SHA-256 are designed to be fast, which is exactly wrong for passwords — an attacker can try billions per second. Password storage needs a deliberately slow algorithm such as bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2, with a per-user salt.

privacy.title: Where the hashing happens
privacy.description: Everything runs in your browser. Text is hashed with the Web Crypto API, files are read locally, and MD5 is computed in JavaScript because Web Crypto deliberately omits it. No input leaves the page.

id-validator.title: ID Number Validator
id-validator.description: Check the checksum of a Hong Kong Identity Card number or a Taiwan National ID, and see what the number encodes. Runs entirely in your browser.

errors.format: That is not a well-formed number.
errors.checksum: The check digit does not match the rest of the number.

id-validator.disclaimer: This checks arithmetic only. A number can pass the checksum and still not belong to anyone. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.

overview.title: What this checks, and what it cannot
overview.description: Both the HKID and the Taiwan National ID carry a check digit derived from the other characters. This tool recomputes it. That catches typos and transcription errors, which is what it is for. It cannot tell you whether a number was ever issued, whether it is currently valid, or who holds it — that requires the issuing authority.

hkid.title: How the HKID check digit works
hkid.description: An HKID is one or two letters, six digits and a check character in parentheses. Letters are valued A=10 through Z=35; a missing first letter counts as 36. The eight body characters are multiplied by weights 9 down to 2, summed, and the check character is whatever makes the total divisible by 11. A remainder of 10 is written as the letter A.

twid.title: How the Taiwan check digit works
twid.description: A Taiwan ID is one letter and nine digits. The letter maps to a two-digit code for the county or city of first household registration. That code contributes its first digit at weight 1 and its second at weight 9; the following eight digits carry weights 8 down to 1, and the final check digit carries weight 1. A valid number sums to a multiple of 10.
twid.gender: The first digit after the letter is the gender marker: 1 for male, 2 for female. Since 2021 the numbers 8 and 9 mark the unified numbers issued to foreign residents.

business-number.title: Business Number Validator
business-number.description: Check a Taiwan unified business number (統一編號) against the Ministry of Finance checksum, including the 2023 rule change. Runs in your browser.

result.sevenRule: Passes under the special rule for a 7 in the seventh position
result.legacyOnly: Valid under the current rule, but not under the pre-2023 rule

errors.format: A unified business number is exactly eight digits.

business-number.disclaimer: This checks arithmetic only. To confirm a company exists, look it up in the Ministry of Finance registry.

overview.title: What a unified business number is
overview.description: The 統一編號 is the eight-digit number Taiwan assigns to every registered business — the equivalent of a company registration number. It appears on invoices, contracts and tax filings, and it carries a checksum so that a mistyped digit can be caught before it reaches your records.

algorithm.title: How the checksum works
algorithm.description: Each of the eight digits is multiplied by a fixed weight: 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 4, 1. Each product is reduced to the sum of its own digits, so 7 × 2 = 14 contributes 5 rather than 14. The number is valid when the total is divisible by 5.
algorithm.seven: There is one exception. When the seventh digit is 7, the product 7 × 4 = 28 may be counted as either 1 or 2, so the number is valid if either the total or the total plus one is divisible by 5.

change.title: The 2023 rule change
change.description: Before April 2023 the total had to be divisible by 10. The Ministry of Finance relaxed this to divisible by 5, roughly doubling the pool of issuable numbers. Every number valid under the old rule is still valid, but a validator written before 2023 will reject numbers that are now legitimate — if an old system is rejecting new companies, this is why.
